The '''Carib Brewery Limited''' is headquartered in [[Trinidad and Tobago]].  It produces ''Carib'' and ''Stag'' beers and a range of [[shandy]] products. The main brewery is located in [[Champs Fleurs]], Trinidad, while Carib also has breweries in [[Saint Kitts and Nevis]] and [[Grenada]], as well as a United States affiliate brewery in [[Cape Canaveral, Florida]].

The brewery is owned by the [[ANSA McAL]] Group of Companies.

== History ==

In order to reduce Trinidad's dependency on the cultivation of sugar and oil, in 1947 the Caribbean Development Company Limited (CDC) was founded. In September 1950 the first Trinidadian beer, Carib lager, was brought to market. The brand is still available, is being sold throughout large parts of the Caribbean and is market leader in Trinidad.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.caribbrewery.com/Corporate/tabid/56/Default.aspx |title=History of Brewing in T&T |publisher=CaribBrewery.com |accessdate=2022-05-31 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150427214658/http://www.caribbrewery.com/Corporate/tabid/56/Default.aspx |archive-date=27 April 2015 |url-status=dead}}</ref> In 1955 CDC was split into Carib Brewery Ltd. (starting with seven employees) and Carib Glassworks Ltd.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.caribbrewery.com/LinkClick.aspx?fileticket=sFvfjeKDuCc%3D&tabid=61 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131029202734/http://www.caribbrewery.com/LinkClick.aspx?fileticket=sFvfjeKDuCc%3D&tabid=61 |archive-date=2013-10-29  | title=Master Brewers Association of the Americas 49th Annual District Caribbean Convention 2010 | publisher=CaribBrewery.com | accessdate=2022-07-25}}</ref> Through acquisitions Carib attained a monopoly on beer production in Trinidad in 1957.

In the 1970s Carib expanded and raised its production to 250,000 hectolitres per year. 1973 the company launched its first non-alcoholic beverage, Malta Carib, a malt beer. In 1985 this was followed up with ''Shandy Carib'', the company's first [[shandy]]. In 1987 the equipment was modernised by renowned German manufacturer [[Krones|Steinecker Maschinenfabrik]] so that the output mark of 1.000.000 hectolitres was surpassed.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.caribbrewery.com/LinkClick.aspx?fileticket=sFvfjeKDuCc%3D&tabid=61 | title=Master Brewers Association of the Americas 49th Annual District Caribbean Convention 2010 | publisher=CaribBrewery.com | accessdate=2022-11-16 | archive-date=2013-10-29 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131029202734/http://www.caribbrewery.com/LinkClick.aspx?fileticket=sFvfjeKDuCc%3D&tabid=61 | url-status=bot: unknown }}</ref> In the subsequent time the company's beverage business was internationalised. On the one hand distribution and licence contracts with foreign producers such as [[Diageo]] or [[InBev]] were concluded, on the other hand Carib started to export its own brands. Production sites outside Trinidad were founded: Carib Brewery [[St. Kitts and Nevis]] exists since 1997, Carib Brewery [[Grenada]] since 2002. In 2015 another shandy was launched, Carib [[Radler]].<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.lime.tt/2015/09/the-launch-of-carib-radler/ | title=The Launch of Carib Radler | publisher=Lime.tt | accessdate=2022-02-20 | archive-date=2020-11-28 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201128130315/http://www.lime.tt/2015/09/the-launch-of-carib-radler/ | url-status=bot: unknown }}</ref>

In 2016 ANSA McAL bought American brewery [[Florida Beer Company]] located in [[Cape Canaveral]]. At first Florida Beer was continued as an individual brand, but in June 2021 it was discontinued. Since then the Carib Brewery brands and a [[craft beer]] called Hurricane Reef are being brewed in the Cape Canaveral facilities.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.clickorlando.com/news/local/2021/09/29/florida-beer-company-in-cape-canaveral-changes-name-to-carib-brewery/#// | title=Florida Beer Company in Cape Canaveral changes name to Carib Brewery | publisher=ClickOrlando.com | accessdate=2023-03-16}}</ref> In late 2024 the company expanded to India, created a [[joint venture]] with local distillery Globus SPirits and started the production of beer for the Indian market.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://newsday.co.tt/2024/10/24/carib-brewery-looks-to-the-east-for-expansion/ | title=Carib Brewery looks to the East for expansion | publisher=Newsday.co.tt | accessdate=2025-01-20}}</ref>

== Products ==

=== Beers ===
[[File:Carib Malta.jpg|thumb|Non-alcoholic Carib Malta beer bottle]]
* ''Carib'', a [[lager]] beer with 5.0% [[alcohol by volume|abv]]. Silver medal in the "low-alcohol lager" category at the [[World Beer Cup]] 2000.<ref name="WBC">{{cite web | url=https://www.worldbeercup.org/winners/award-winners/ | title=Award Winners | publisher=WorldBeerCup.org | accessdate=2022-05-19}}</ref>
* ''Carib Pilsner Light'', a [[pilsner]] with 4% abv.
* ''Guinness Foreign Extra Stout'', a [[Beer classification in Sweden and Finland|strong beer]] with 7.5% abv, bottling agreement with [[Diageo]].
* ''Heineken'', a lager beer with 5% abv, bottling agreement with [[Heineken]].
* ''Heineken 0.0'', a [[Low-alcohol beer|non-alcoholic beer]], bottling agreement with Heineken.
* ''Heineken Light'', a [[light beer]] with 3.3% abv, bottling agreement with Heineken.
* ''Hurricane Reef'', an [[India Pale Ale|IPA]] with 6.5% abv, brewed by Carib USA.
* ''Mackeson Triple Stout'', a [[Stout#Milk stout|sweet stout]] with 4.9% abv, bottling agreement with [[InBev]].
* ''Malta Carib'', a [[malt beer]].
* ''Pola Beer'', a lager beer with 5% abv.
* ''Royal Extra Stout'', a strong beer with 6.6% abv with added [[caramel]].
* ''Shandy Carib'', a [[shandy]] in four flavours (lime, ginger, tangerine and [[Roselle (plant)|sorrel]]).
* ''Smalta'', a malt beer.
* ''Stag'', a lager beer with 5.2% abv. Gold medal in the "low-alcohol lager" category at the World Beer Cup 2000.<ref name="WBC" />

=== Other beverages ===
* ''Caribe'', a [[cider]] with flavours Brut, Mimosa, Pearsecco and Rosé.
* ''Ginseng Up'', a soda with [[ginseng]] extractives and fruit flavour. Flavours: Original, Lemon Lime and [[Kola Champagne]].
* ''Rockstone Tonic Wine'', a [[Fortified wine|tonic wine]].<ref>{{cite web | url=https://newsday.co.tt/2022/08/20/carib-brewery-adds-tonic-wine-to-beverage-line/ | title=Carib Brewery adds tonic wine to beverage line | publisher=Newsday.co.tt | accessdate=2022-12-20}}</ref>
* ''[[Smirnoff]] Ice'', a [[vodka]]-based mixed drink, bottling agreement with Diageo.

=== Former products ===
* ''Carib Radler'', a [[radler]] with 2% abv, that is occasionally produced seasonally.
